title: ASEAN
points: Established 8 August 1967 (Bangkok Declaration)
Headquarters: Jakarta, Indonesia
Founding members: Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand; later Brunei, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Cambodia (10 members)
Timor-Leste was admitted as the 11th member in October 2025
India is a Sectoral Partner (1992) → Dialogue Partner (1996) → Summit-level partner (2002); 'Act East Policy' anchors ties

title: World Trade Organization (WTO)
points: Headquarters: Geneva, Switzerland
Established 1 January 1995; successor to GATT (1947)
Highest decision-making body: Ministerial Conference (meets at least every two years)
Disputes are settled by the Dispute Settlement Body; the Appellate Body has been non-functional since December 2019

title: United Nations
points: Founded 24 October 1945 (UN Charter); Headquarters: New York
193 member states
Six principal organs: General Assembly, Security Council, ECOSOC, Trusteeship Council, ICJ, Secretariat
UNSC: 5 permanent members (US, UK, France, Russia, China) with veto + 10 non-permanent members elected for 2-year terms

title: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
points: Headquarters: Washington, D.C.
Created at the Bretton Woods Conference (1944); formally came into existence in 1945 and began financial operations in 1947
Publishes the World Economic Outlook and Global Financial Stability Report
SDR (Special Drawing Right) is its reserve asset

title: World Bank
points: Headquarters: Washington, D.C.
Born at Bretton Woods (1944) as IBRD
World Bank Group: IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA, ICSID
Publishes the Ease of Doing Business (discontinued 2021), World Development Report, Human Capital Index

title: NATO
points: Established 4 April 1949 (North Atlantic Treaty, Washington)
Headquarters: Brussels, Belgium
Article 5: collective defence — an attack on one is an attack on all
Sweden became the 32nd member in March 2024

title: BRICS
points: Originally Brazil, Russia, India, China (BRIC); South Africa joined in 2010
Expanded from 2024 to include more members (Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE; Indonesia joined in 2025)
New Development Bank (NDB) headquartered in Shanghai
India held the BRICS chair in 2016 and 2021

title: Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)
points: Founded 2001 in Shanghai; Secretariat in Beijing
India and Pakistan became full members in 2017
Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS) is based in Tashkent

title: QUAD
points: Members: India, USA, Japan, Australia
Informal strategic forum centred on a free, open, inclusive Indo-Pacific
Leaders-level summits began in 2021

title: G20
points: Formed 1999 after the Asian financial crisis; leaders' summits since 2008
India held the G20 Presidency in 2023 (New Delhi Leaders' Declaration)
The African Union was admitted as a permanent member at the 2023 New Delhi Summit
No permanent secretariat; presidency rotates annually (troika system)

title: G7
points: Members: Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, United Kingdom, United States (EU participates)
Annual summit hosted by rotating presidency
Informal grouping; no permanent secretariat

title: International Court of Justice (ICJ)
points: Principal judicial organ of the UN; seat: The Hague (Peace Palace), Netherlands
15 judges elected for 9-year terms by the UNGA and UNSC
Decides disputes between States and gives advisory opinions; only States can be parties

title: International Criminal Court (ICC)
points: Seat: The Hague, Netherlands
Rome Statute adopted 1998; entered into force 1 July 2002
Tries individuals for genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and aggression
India is not a party to the Rome Statute; the ICC is not a UN organ

title: World Health Organization (WHO)
points: Headquarters: Geneva; constituted 7 April 1948 (World Health Day)
Specialised agency of the UN
Governing body: World Health Assembly

title: UNESCO
points: Headquarters: Paris; founded 1945
Maintains the World Heritage List under the 1972 World Heritage Convention
Also runs Intangible Cultural Heritage lists

title: International Labour Organization (ILO)
points: Headquarters: Geneva; founded 1919 (Treaty of Versailles)
Unique tripartite structure: governments, employers, workers
Became a UN specialised agency in 1946

title: Ramsar Convention on Wetlands
points: Adopted 2 February 1971 in Ramsar, Iran; in force 1975
World Wetlands Day is observed on 2 February
Secretariat located in Gland, Switzerland
Montreux Record lists Ramsar sites facing ecological change (Keoladeo and Loktak are on it)

title: UNFCCC, Kyoto & Paris Agreement
points: UNFCCC adopted 1992 (Rio Earth Summit); in force 1994; secretariat in Bonn
Kyoto Protocol 1997 — binding emission targets for developed countries
Paris Agreement adopted at COP21 (2015), in force 4 November 2016 — hold warming well below 2°C, pursue 1.5°C
Parties submit Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)

title: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
points: Established 1 April 1935 (RBI Act, 1934); nationalised 1 January 1949; HQ Mumbai
Monetary Policy Committee: 6 members (3 from RBI, 3 external); statutory since 2016
Inflation target: 4% with a ±2% tolerance band (CPI)
Repo rate = rate at which RBI lends short-term to banks

title: SEBI
keywords: securities and exchange board of india
points: Established 1988; statutory powers via SEBI Act, 1992; HQ Mumbai
Regulator of the securities market in India

title: NITI Aayog
points: Set up 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission
Chairperson: Prime Minister; policy think tank (non-statutory)
Publishes the SDG India Index, India Innovation Index, Multidimensional Poverty Index (national)

title: NPCI & UPI
points: NPCI established 2008 as umbrella entity for retail payments
UPI launched in April 2016
Also runs RuPay, IMPS, NACH, FASTag

title: ISRO
points: Established 15 August 1969; HQ Bengaluru
Chandrayaan-3 soft-landed near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023 (observed as National Space Day)
Gaganyaan is India's human spaceflight programme

title: Parliament of India
points: Lok Sabha: maximum 550 members (543 elected currently); Rajya Sabha: maximum 250 (238 elected + 12 nominated)
President summons, prorogues, and may dissolve the Lok Sabha
Money Bills (Art. 110) can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha

title: Supreme Court of India
points: Inaugurated 28 January 1950; Article 124 provides for its establishment
Sanctioned strength: 34 judges (CJI + 33) since 2019
Judges retire at 65; High Court judges at 62
Article 142: complete justice; Article 32: writs for Fundamental Rights

title: New criminal codes (BNS, BNSS, BSA)
points: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita replaced the IPC; Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita replaced the CrPC; Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam replaced the Indian Evidence Act
All three came into force on 1 July 2024

title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
points: Enacted August 2023 (Presidential assent 11 August 2023)
Creates the Data Protection Board of India
Rooted in the right to privacy recognised in Puttaswamy (2017)

title: Women's Reservation (106th Amendment)
points: Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023 — Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam
Reserves one-third of seats in Lok Sabha and State Assemblies for women
Operationalisation is linked to the next Census and delimitation

title: Election Commission of India
points: Constitutional body under Article 324; HQ New Delhi
Conducts elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President
CEC & Other ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service) Act, 2023: selection committee = PM, Leader of Opposition, a Union Cabinet Minister

title: NHRC
points: Statutory body under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993; established 12 October 1993
Chairperson is a former Chief Justice of India (or SC judge)

title: NALSA
points: Constituted under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987
Implements Article 39A (equal justice and free legal aid)
Patron-in-Chief: CJI

title: Competition Commission of India (CCI)
points: Established under the Competition Act, 2002 (functional since 2009)
Prevents anti-competitive agreements, abuse of dominance and regulates combinations

title: Law Commission of India
points: Non-statutory, executive body constituted by the Government for a fixed tenure
First Law Commission (1955) was chaired by M.C. Setalvad
Recommends legal reforms to the Ministry of Law and Justice

title: Bharat Ratna & Padma Awards
points: Both instituted in 1954
Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian honour; Padma order: Vibhushan > Bhushan > Shri
Announced around Republic Day; Article 18(1) bars titles — these are not 'titles' as per the Balaji Raghavan (1996) ruling

title: Nobel Prizes
points: First awarded 1901; Peace Prize presented in Oslo, others in Stockholm
Economics prize (Sveriges Riksbank Prize) added in 1969
Announced every October; presented 10 December

title: Project Tiger & NTCA
points: Project Tiger launched 1973
National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) is statutory (Wildlife (Protection) Amendment, 2006)
Tiger estimation is conducted every 4 years

title: Constitutional offices (quick table)
points: Attorney General – Art. 76; CAG – Art. 148; Governor – Art. 153; Finance Commission – Art. 280; UPSC – Art. 315; Election Commission – Art. 324
